newsitem.title: JAPAN: ASIAN METALS - JAPAN ZINC PREMIUMS SEEN EASING.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN METALS - JAPAN ZINC PREMIUMS SEEN EASING.

text.p: Japan's spot zinc premiums are likely to ease slightly next week as supplies in the Asian market appear ample, Japanese traders said on Wednesday.
Japan's physical zinc business has ground to a halt, discouraged by a wide three months/cash backwardation on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and Japan's "Obon" holidays, they said.

"There has been little spot activity amid the summer lull, with virtually no spot deals in the past few days. I have a feeling that Japan's zinc premiums may dip slightly after the holidays," a trader at a trading house said.
"As Japan's galvanized steel-sheet makers have now finished covering most of their near-term requirements, the current tightness at home may ease gradually toward the autumn," he said.
Another trader said: "With such a backwardation, Japanese buyers, afraid of holding excessive inventories, are not in a hurry to buy in the spot market.
Cash/three-months backwardations on the LME on Tuesday remained wide at around $115/125 compared to $115/165 on Monday.
"Given an increase in Singapore warehouse stocks, supplies are quite ample in the Asian market. I think China is likely to offer off-grade zinc aggressively," the trader said.
Taiwan traders said on Tuesday that the country's spot zinc premiums had fallen sharply due to sluggish local demand.
Zinc on LME fell steeply after a 1,400-tonne stock increase that gave credence to talk of Chinese shipments of some 20,000 tonnes of metal to Singapore.
In aluminium, a fall in prices on the LME and the yen's firmer tendency, are not expected to lure active Japanese buying, traders said.
"Domestic aluminium demand is set to dip as the peak demand season draws to an end," one aluminium trader said.
Aluminium premiums were little changed from last week at $80-85 per tonne.
Traders said they were focusing on price negotiations due to start later this month on fourth-quarter deliveries.
They said they expect premiums for the fourth quarter to be lower than third-quarter premiums ranging from $86 to $90.
"We hope premiums will be about $5.00 lower than the previous (third) quarter," one aluminium trader said.

Japanese traders expect aluminium prices on the LME to fall further after sharp losses on Tuesday overnight, and said that a correction was long overdue after the strong rally over the past several days.
The domestic copper market was quiet amid lacklustre domestic demand.
